text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — inference-prod: 5xx surge (error rate > 6% for 5m). Paging primary oncall. See incident summary: https://grafana.example.com/d/inf-prod/errors

alex: I'm primary, saw the alert. I'm going to start triage but heads-up — I have a handoff in 40min. Leaving 18:30 PT.

maya: @alex I can be secondary but I have a red-eye flight tonight, boarding at 18:45 PT. I can cover initial escalation until takeoff but may be unreachable for ~90m once airborne.

alex: thanks. we need a clear swap plan. @lee — can you be backup if this becomes a Sev2 and maya is offline?

lee: I can. If it's Sev2 or customer-impacting I'll jump in. For now follow the runbook and alert policy.

alex: Triage notes so far (quick):
- Error spike correlates with request latency on rtr-inference nodes 3/7
- No recent deploys in last 2 hours (CI webhook shows nothing)
- Rate-limiter shows no bursts from a single customer

alex: Immediate next steps (assigning):
- @maya check model-worker logs and KV cache errors (tail on node 3)
- @alex check GPU memory pressure and restart worker if stuck
- run the quick health check and note customer impact

maya: tailing logs now: seeing repeated "kvCache: miss->timeout" and "rpc: connection reset by peer" on node-3.

alex: run these checks and paste outputs if you can:```bash
# check prometheus error rate
curl -s "https://prometheus/api/v1/query?query=sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"inference\",status=~\"5..\"}[5m]))"
# check worker process status
sudo systemctl status redwood-worker@3
# quick restart if mem/bad state
sudo systemctl restart redwood-worker@3 && journalctl -u redwood-worker@3 -n 200 --no-pager
```

maya: ran the status, posting last lines: "OOM killer invoked for python3 (worker)" and repeated grpc errors. Restarted the service once, it came back but errors resumed after ~3m.

alex: that suggests a memory leak or bad model batch. I'm going to scale the worker pool down temporarily and enable no-batching mode for the affected model. Doing commands now.

alex: scaling down and toggling config:```json
{"model":"mosaic-13b","batching":"off","max_instances":2}
```

incident-bot: note: config change applied by alex at 2026-03-14T18:02:10Z.

maya: after disabling batching, error rate dropped to ~1.2% over the last 2m. Latency increased ~120ms per request but customer impact looks reduced.

alex: ok good. Here's the temporary on-call handoff plan:
- I'm primary until 18:30 PT (thread owner for any outstanding issues).
- @maya will be secondary until 18:45 PT then possibly unavailable during flight.
- @lee will be the fallback (pageable) from 18:45 PT onward.

Escalation / paging rules (clarified here, follow these exactly):
1) Page primary (current oncall) for any alert labeled P0/P1 or >5min steady error >5%.
2) If no ack within 2 minutes OR if incident escalates (customer-facing or data-loss), page secondary and set bridge.
3) If unresolved after 10 minutes OR if service degradation increases, page SRE Lead @lee immediately and create an incident bridge.
4) If incident causes active customer outages (>=1 major customer SLA breach), page Eng Manager @samira and Exec Ops.

Paging channels / addresses: page via PagerDuty -> oncall rotation (primary). If PD fails, call @lee at +1-555-0102. Do NOT page infra-oncall unless asked by SRE Lead.

alex: additional handoff checklist for the person taking over:
- Confirm metrics baseline in Grafana (errors, latency, qps).
- Confirm runbook section used: ops-runbooks: inference > memory / KV cache (link: https://confluence.example.com/ops/inference/memory-kvcache)
- Capture commands run and revert plan (we disabled batching — document rollback criteria).
- Notify support & product if degraded for >20m (template in runbook).

ops-runbooks: runbook link and checklist acknowledged. Recommend creating a short eval of the model input distribution if errors reappear after rollback.

maya: leaving handoff notes in the runbook page. I'll monitor PD notifications until boarding. If I miss anything, @lee please step in.

lee: acknowledged. I'll be on standby and will create the incident bridge if error creeps back over 4% or if any major customer complains.

alex: final — we consider this a mitigated incident for now (error dropped from 6.8% -> 1.2%). Keeping the thread open until 19:30 PT for postmortem notes and decision on permanent fix. If error resurfaces, follow escalation above. :white_check_mark:

samira: thanks for the clear plan. If you end up paging me, include customer impact estimate and list of key customers affected.

incident-bot: incident status updated: mitigated -> monitoring. All changes logged.

alex: handing off. I will update handoff doc and mark primary as 'off-duty' at 18:30 PT. Good catch everyone.
